body_markdown:
A long time ago, friends Duane Wylder and Jim Rockstead dreamed up the notion of running a regular weeknight motocross series under stadium lights—something that could be both inexpensive and easily accessible. The empty infield at Portland International Raceway was the ideal place, and[Thursday Night Motocross](https://www.thursdaynightmotocross.com/) became an instant it.


This year marked the 60th anniversary of the series—the longest-running weekly moto event in the country—and today, Wylder’s sons Rick and Ron run the show. I’ve been out a few times in past seasons to spectate and always had[a great time](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorcycles/tired-of-speed-parades-and-gimmicky-races-check-out-supercross/) . Entry is just $10, it’s never too crowded, and you have access to the entire perimeter of the track, so the viewing experience is fantastic.


[Stefan Lombard](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/stefan-lombard/)


[Stefan Lombard](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/stefan-lombard/)


[Stefan Lombard](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/stefan-lombard/)


I had it on my calendar to get out there when the season kicked off in April, then in May, then June… Surely I’d make it for the official celebration in July? But then it was September 24, the final event of this landmark season, and I still hadn’t gone. So last Thursday I dug out my camera and a handful of lenses I hadn’t shot with in a while, and I headed across town to make good on that promise to myself.


Nearly 200 riders turned out to compete in 16 classes under the lights, from 4-year-olds on little 50cc cuties to stiff old Gen Xers on 250s.

I shoot micro 4/3 on an Olympus, which in today’s photographic landscape is essentially the Hodaka two-stroke of cameras. The sensor is tiny and can suffer in low light, but it’s a system I love, the weather was great, and it was joyful to just be out there with no obligations to anyone but myself as I searched for fun angles and[colorful chaos](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/high-flying-dirt-slinging-ama-supermotocross-makes-f1-look-pedestrian/) . Even when the weather turned not so great, the rain only added to the experience. Until I was just soaked and cold, that is. But by then it was after 9 p.m. and I’d shot so many photos, I knew I’d be digging myself out of them through the weekend, so it felt like the right time leave the party.


A party, I should say, that will pick up again next April. Thursday nights under the lights, as always.
